title: Anthropic's Record $81.3 Billion IPO Opens 34% Higher, Then Fades to a 17% Gain
excerpt: The Claude maker's Nasdaq debut briefly valued it at about $2 trillion on a fully diluted basis, surpassing SpaceX's listing as the largest IPO on record.
body:
• Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, November 19 — 34% above the $83 IPO price — and closed at $97.17, up 17% on the day, Reuters reported.
  • The company sold 980 million shares at $83, raising $81.3 billion and surpassing the $75 billion SpaceX collected at its June listing, making it the largest IPO on record.
  • At the opening price, Anthropic's fully diluted valuation reached about $2 trillion; based on outstanding shares, its value reached as much as $1.5 trillion, on par with Tesla.
  • For investors, the debut is now the public benchmark for frontier AI valuations — and its first-day fade, on a day Wall Street's main indexes sank, is the caution attached to it.

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI chatbot, notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, November 19, edging past SpaceX's June listing and capping a turbulent stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology, Reuters reported. The shares, trading under the ticker ANT, opened at $111.50, 34 per cent higher than the $83 IPO price set on Wednesday, but pared gains through the session and ended the day at $97.17, up 17 per cent.

The fully diluted $2 trillion valuation includes stock options and restricted stock units promised to employees but not yet vested. Based on outstanding shares, the company's value reached as much as $1.5 trillion on Thursday, on par with Tesla. Anthropic is the first large frontier AI model maker to go public, which makes its pricing the sector's first public benchmark.

The offering

Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing above the $70 to $78 range set when it launched the road show, and raised $81.3 billion — surpassing the $75 billion SpaceX collected at its June listing and making this the largest IPO on record. A separate $26 billion private placement from major technology companies, including Nvidia, took the total raised to $107.3 billion, CNN reported. The massive offering will earn the underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a $550 million fee, according to a regulatory filing cited by Reuters.

Based on the IPO price, chief executive Dario Amodei and his six co-founders, who together own about 10 per cent of the company, held stakes worth nearly $150 billion combined, according to a Reuters calculation based on the filing. The listing is set to create thousands of paper millionaires among employees, rewarding everyone from early researchers to administrative staff.

"Debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future."

— Dario Amodei, Anthropic CEO, to CNBC on Thursday

Growth, losses and the $900 billion question

Anthropic's net loss narrowed in the third quarter as revenue jumped 47 per cent from the previous quarter, even as the pace of growth slowed sharply from the prior quarter, Reuters reported. The company has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google — the spending at the centre of the debate over whether the AI boom is becoming a bubble, as soaring valuations and circular deals among AI developers, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors fuel questions about the durability of the industry's growth.

Analysts quoted by Reuters were split on what the debut proves. Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research, called the launch a critical step in reassuring the market about AI's potential but "really just the beginning," with OpenAI's plans and Anthropic's own trading history still to come. Talley Leger, chief market strategist at The Wealth Consulting Group, said Anthropic "isn't a prudent 'buy-at-any-price' opportunity for retail wealth clients," noting that retail investors buying hot technology IPOs on day one have historically underperformed broad market indexes over a three-year horizon.

What to watch next

The debut came on a day when Wall Street's main indexes sank, and follow-on coverage has noted that the listing did not revive the wider AI trade. What happens next turns on Anthropic's first earnings reports as a public company, whether it taps the debt markets Amodei pointed to, and how the stock holds its $83 issue price as the initial euphoria settles. CNN's account of the offering sets out the pricing and the accompanying private placement in detail.
